newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica P.M. to visit Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica P.M. to visit Cuba.

text.p: Jamaican Prime Minister P.J. Patterson will lead a diplomatic and trade mission to Cuba Wednesday, the first visit by a Jamaican head of government in 20 years.

The last Jamaican prime minister to travel to Havana to meet with Cuban President Fidel Castro was the late Michael Manley, who visited in 1977. Patterson accompanied him on that trip as Jamaica's foreign minister.
But in contrast with the socialist rhetoric of that visit, this week's visit was to include several Jamaican business leaders, who hope for trade with the Communist-ruled island.

The leaders of Barbados and St. Vincent also were to visit Cuba within the next several weeks, before an upcoming summit of the 14-member Caribbean Community, during which leaders from the English-speaking Caribbean are expected to decide whether to negotiate a free trade accord with Cuba, as well as to admit Haiti as the group's 15th member.
